vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: Untrusted plugin source can evade static string/AST checks and then import dangerous modules such as sys, shutil, multiprocessing, importlib, and pickle. The runtime sandbox originally had no import denylist; later PluginImportGuard blocked only ctypes, __builtin__, __builtins__, subprocess, os, and capability-gated socket, so the named modules still reached Python import execution.

atomic_bic.evidence: 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef is the first public commit that adds plugin_manager.py and plugin_sandbox.py, loads attacker-supplied plugin modules, and executes plugin code while restricting only selected builtins/socket/subprocess entry points and providing no runtime import guard. Its parent 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a has no plugin_system paths. e588aaa3a53ef291406b02745c20fdea8cea7f7c is a later security remediation that adds a partial import guard; 50bec5d3656d62b8dbbb0ce082fd67b8436677fd later adds the larger AST list and makes the two-list mismatch explicit. Neither later hardening commit is the first vulnerable writer.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: git cat-file against 649f737a9f04645508d079c0c772a8a2b4c7457a confirms both openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_manager.py and plugin_sandbox.py are absent; 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef is a single-parent commit that adds both paths.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef is a large single-parent feature object, but all fetched origin heads and path histories identify it as the first surviving public writer, and GitHub's commit-to-pulls endpoint returns no associated PR or reconstructable member commits. No finer public member is available, so the surviving object is the atomic auditable BIC; decomposed_shas remains empty.

affected_fixed_release_membership.evidence: Tag ancestry shows v1.2.1 lacks 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef, v1.3.0 through v1.3.6 contain that BIC but not e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092, and v1.4.0 contains both. Thus the repository-supported vulnerable release window is >=1.3.0,<1.4.0 and v1.4.0 is fixed. The PUBLISHED CNA record's semver range 0..<1.4.0 has the correct upper boundary but an overbroad lower boundary.

direct_fix_or_unpatched_state.evidence: At e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092^ the runtime ALWAYS_BLOCKED set and AST DANGEROUS_MODULES set differ. The single-parent e0c999ea44429e8de00b4acb3ba570efdc733092 commit creates plugin_security_constants.py and makes both checks consume BLOCKED_MODULES, directly closing the named list-desynchronization path; v1.4.0 contains this commit.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: The corrected BIC commit object 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef contains both the Generated with Claude Code marker and Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>. AI attribution therefore remains AI_ROOT_CAUSE based only on the corrected BIC, independently of AI markers on e588aaa, 50bec5d, or the fix.

findings: Primary misidentifies e588aaa3a53ef291406b02745c20fdea8cea7f7c as the BIC even though that commit is a partial security remediation of the already-vulnerable plugin execution path introduced by 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef.

50bec5d3656d62b8dbbb0ce082fd67b8436677fd first makes the advisory's two-list mismatch explicit by adding DANGEROUS_MODULES, but it also hardens a pre-existing bypass rather than introducing the underlying ability of plugin code to reach unblocked imports.
The corrected BIC remains Claude-coauthored, so the causal verdict stays AI_ROOT_CAUSE while the introducer, parent, flaw-origin narrative, and BIC AI marker must change.
The CNA affected range starts at version 0, but local release ancestry proves the plugin system and corrected BIC first ship in v1.3.0; the evidence-supported range is >=1.3.0,<1.4.0.

corrected_fields.flaw_origin: 8a5ed7e62417441ed98b39481ac1a47510c1a9ef first added the plugin loading and sandbox execution paths. Its validation only warned on a short literal-pattern list and its sandbox replaced selected builtins.open, socket.socket, and subprocess.Popen entry points without an import denylist, leaving dangerous modules reachable. Later f4b55e6 added strict literal blocking, e588aaa added a partial runtime import guard, and 50bec5d added the larger AST DANGEROUS_MODULES policy; these were incomplete remediations/hardening of the existing flaw. e0c999e directly synchronized both lists.
